column5: Attack on AI agents' external resources
column9: A skill is an external resource used by an agent, and AST01 covers skills intentionally created with malicious payloads.

column5: Attack on AI agents' external resources
column9: Both risks cover attacks on external components or services that an agent relies on to perform its tasks.
Excessive skill permissions increase the actions available after an agent or skill is compromised or misused.
Over-privileged skills can access sensitive information and expose it to tools or agents outside the intended scope.
Deceptive or unsafe metadata exploits the trust boundary between the skill publisher, loader, agent, and installer.
Both risks involve instructions embedded in external content that can cause an AI system to perform unintended actions.
Missing file-system, credential, and network boundaries can expose sensitive information to a skill and its connected tools.
Both risks concern keeping agent components and dependencies in a known, secure, and supported state.
Traditional scanners can measure the wrong properties and miss behavior that emerges from code and natural-language instructions together.
Missing ownership, approval, and audit processes make it difficult to assign responsibility for actions taken through installed skills.
Missing skill-level audit trails make the source of agent actions difficult to trace.
Differences in platform metadata and control enforcement can cause the same skill to behave differently after it is ported.
